summary: J. A. B. van Buitenen worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1953) under Jan Gonda (~1948–1953), holding posts at Utrecht University (~1953–1956) and the University of Chicago (~1959–1979).
J. B. Disanayaka is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held posts at the University of Colombo (~1968–2002) and SOAS University of London (attested 1996).

J. C. Cleary specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Harvard University (~1971–1980) under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi (attested 1986) and served as an instructor at Wesleyan University.
J. Estlin Carpenter worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of London (~1860–1866) and held a post at the University of Oxford (~1889–1915).
J. G. de Casparis worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts as professor at Leiden University (attested 1987) and at SOAS University of London (attested 1991).

Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham–Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University. He directed the Institute for the Study of American Religion (~1969) and held posts at UC Santa Barbara (~1985–2011) and Baylor University (~2011).
J. Talboys Wheeler worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford and served as Assistant Secretary for the Government of India (~1862–1876).
Jack Kornfield is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at Dartmouth College (~1963–1967). He held a post at the Spirit Rock Meditation Center (~1987).
Jack Laughlin works in Indology and religious studies. He completed a PhD at McMaster University in 1999 and held a post at the University of Sudbury.

Jacob Dalton specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan (-2002) under Donald S. Lopez Jr., later holding posts at SOAS, Yale University (2005), and UC Berkeley (attested 2011).
Jacob Holubeck is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under supervisor Kirill Jurievitch Solonin (attested 2013).
Jacob N. Kinnard works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held posts as Assistant Professor of Religion at William & Mary and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Indologist Jacob Samuel Speyer studied under Hendrik Kern (~1868–1872). He held posts at the University of Amsterdam (1877–1889), University of Groningen (1889–1903), and as Professor of Indology at Leiden University (1903–1913).

Jacob Wackernagel worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Göttingen (~1872–1874) under Theodor Benfey. He held posts as professor at the University of Basel (1881–1902) and at the University of Göttingen (~1902–1915).

Jacqueline I. Stone works in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at San Francisco State University and UCLA, she served as a professor at Princeton University (~1990–2019) and president of the Society for the Study of Japanese Religions (~1997–1999).

Jacqueline Suthren Hirst is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who completed doctoral research under Julius Lipner (attested 2005). She held a post at the University of Manchester (attested 2005).
Jacques Bacot was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. He held academic posts at the University of Paris and at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1936–1954).

Jacques Gernet studied at the University of Algiers 1 and ENLOV. In Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at CNRS (1950), EHESS (~1955–1968), Paris-Sorbonne, Collège de France (1975–1992), and Paris Diderot University (attested 1988).

Jacques Giès worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at Paris-Sorbonne University and Beaux-Arts de Paris, serving as Chief Curator of Chinese Painting at Musée Guimet (~1980–2008).

Jacques May specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He served as editor-in-chief at Hōbōgirin (~1962–1978) and École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1962–1981), and as professor at the University of Lausanne (~1977–1992).
